Daily Brief

The day's most consequential developments center on shifting security alignments and escalating crises. In a significant challenge to Ukrainian unity during wartime, former Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov called for presidential elections, marking the first such demand by a major political figure since Russia's 2022 invasion [BBC, France 24, Al Jazeera]. Meanwhile, the US-South Korea alliance faces strain as Washington requested cutting joint military exercises from eleven to five days, with President Trump citing his relationship with Kim Jong Un and reportedly seeking a summit before year's end [BBC, Al Jazeera, Nikkei Asia]. In a last-minute reprieve for North American trade, Trump paused planned 50% tariffs on Canadian goods for three days as both sides work toward a deal that could include revival of the Keystone XL pipeline [BBC]. The DRC's Ebola outbreak has become the deadliest in the country's history with over 2,325 deaths, spreading to a sixth province while health authorities warn it has not yet peaked [RFI, The Guardian]. Regional tensions persist as Israel struck a Syrian airbase, drawing Turkish condemnation after the US blamed Israel for defying American efforts to support Damascus's new government [France 24, Le Monde].

Top Stories
01 Geopolitics

Former Ukrainian Defence Minister Fedorov Calls for Wartime Elections in Direct Challenge to Zelensky

  • Mykhailo Fedorov, dismissed as defence minister in July after six months in post, called for wartime presidential elections in a YouTube video on Tuesday
  • Fedorov stated 'democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia' and urged finding a legal mechanism for elections during ongoing war—the first such demand by a major Ukrainian figure since 2022
  • His dismissal sparked nationwide protests and is widely attributed to tensions with then-army commander Oleksandr Syrskyi, who was also later replaced
  • Zelensky has not responded; Ukrainian law currently prohibits elections under martial law

02 Geopolitics

US and South Korea Cut Joint Military Exercises by Half After Trump Orders Reduction

  • Annual Ulchi Freedom Shield drills reduced from 11 days to 5 at US request, ending August 21 instead of August 27
  • Trump cited exercises as 'costly' and 'hostile' toward North Korea, referencing his 'good relationship' with Kim Jong Un
  • South Korean officials said neither Seoul nor Washington had advance notice of Trump's decision; second phase involving counterattack operations reportedly cancelled
  • Trump is reportedly pushing for an in-person meeting with Kim before year's end; North Korea denounced drills as 'immediate and open threat' without acknowledging the reduction

03 Economics

Trump Pauses 50% Tariffs on Canada as Trade Deal Nears Completion

  • President Trump announced three-day pause on 50% tariffs covering nearly $20 billion in Canadian imports, set to take effect August 19
  • Trump declared the two countries have reached a deal 'subject to finalization of documents'; Canadian PM Mark Carney confirmed 'substantial progress' with 'important work still to be done'
  • Key issues included US auto tariffs and Canadian provincial bans on American liquor sales
  • Trump suggested final deal could allow revival of Keystone XL pipeline, previously blocked by Obama and Biden administrations

04 Climate

DRC Ebola Outbreak Becomes Deadliest in Country's History, Spreads to Sixth Province

  • Death toll reaches at least 2,325 from 4,945 confirmed cases as of August 15, surpassing 2018-2020 outbreak which was previously the worst in DRC history
  • Outbreak is killing approximately one person every 30 minutes; transmission active across 55 health zones in six provinces
  • No approved vaccines or treatments exist for the rare Bundibugyo strain responsible for current outbreak
  • WHO director general stated outbreak is on track to surpass 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (11,325 deaths) as deadliest in history

  • Israel struck an air base in Syria that Turkey was reportedly preparing to use, according to US officials who blamed Israel for the attack
  • Turkey rejected Israeli allegations that it posed a threat by planning to send troops to the base
  • The strike marked extraordinary defiance of the United States, which has sought to support Syria's new government led by a former jihadist allied with Turkey
